19: ## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
20: 
21: Step 2 of the spec folder write recipe shows an `mv` command whose destination line is a bare `<spec-folder>` placeholder. A reader who copies the block has to invent the one value the block does not supply, and a reader who copies it literally gets a shell syntax error. 22: 
23: **Key Decisions**: one known row carries both the destination and the sentence, applied by the shared exactly-once applier.
24: 
25: **Critical Dependencies**: the applier from 054 phase 002 and the verified ledger from 054 phase 001.

54: **Dependencies**:
55: - This phase runs after 054 phase 002 saves `scratch/tools/apply_row.py`, and T001 stops the phase when that file is missing.

59: **Deliverables**:
60: - The fixed Step 2 block in the recipe.
61: - `scratch/known-rows.jsonl`: the known row in the applier schema.
62: - `scratch/census.txt` and `scratch/recheck.txt`: the ledger sweep and the recheck.
63: - `scratch/review/T009.txt`: the read-only frontier review.

66: - When this phase closes, refresh the matching file in ../changelog/ using the parent packet number plus this phase folder name.

72: ## 2. PROBLEM & PURPOSE
73: 
74: ### Problem Statement
75: Step 2 of `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/workflows/spec-folder-write-recipe.md` moves the scaffold into the selected track. The `mv` block names a real source, `specs/078-opencode-authoring-recipe`, and then a destination line of two spaces and `<spec-folder>`. The placeholder is the only value a reader must invent, and nothing in the block says what to put there. A reader who copies the block literally gets a shell syntax error on the destination line. A reader who pauses to interpret it has left the recipe.
76: 
77: ### Purpose
78: The block runs as written with the example track, and one sentence tells the reader which part to change.
79: <!-- /ANCHOR:problem -->
80: 
81: ---
82: 
83: <!-- ANCHOR:scope -->
84: ## 3. SCOPE
85: 
86: ### In Scope
87: - Replace `  <spec-folder>` with `  specs/system-speckit/078-opencode-authoring-recipe`.
88: - Add one sentence after the block that names the track as an example and tells the reader to substitute the track they selected.
89: - Apply every ledger row with `owner_phase` `041-006` whose evidence still reproduces, with the shared applier.
90: - One read-only frontier review at close.
91: 
92: ### Out of Scope
93: - The `<folder>` placeholders in Steps 3, 4, 5 and 6. They are the same class in different steps, and each needs its own reading of the command. They are listed in `goal.md` section 4 as adjacent findings.
94: - The `<spec-folder>` destination in `references/debugging/troubleshooting.md` line 304. It is the same class in another file, and no ledger row owns it here.
95: - The commit hook, sk-git, any template or validator change, and any other file in the 041 series.
96: 
97: ### Files to Change
98: 
99: | File Path | Change Type | Description |
100: |-----------|-------------|-------------|
101: | `.skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/references/workflows/spec-folder-write-recipe.md` | Modify | Replace the bare destination and add the track sentence |
102: | `scratch/known-rows.jsonl` | Create | The known row in the applier schema |
103: | `tasks.md`, `goal.md`, `acceptance-criteria.md`, `implementation-summary.md` | Modify | Progress and evidence |
104: <!-- /ANCHOR:scope -->
105:

109: ## 4. REQUIREMENTS
110: 
111: ### P0 - Blockers (MUST complete)
112: 
113: | ID | Requirement |
114: |----|-------------|
115: | REQ-001 | The recipe holds no `  <spec-folder>` line and holds `  specs/system-speckit/078-opencode-authoring-recipe`. |
116: | REQ-002 | One sentence directly after the Step 2 code block says the track is an example and the reader substitutes the track they selected. |
117: | REQ-003 | Every ledger row with `owner_phase` `041-006` ends as `APPLIED` or `SKIP-GONE`, and no such row's evidence still reproduces. |
118: | REQ-004 | The only path changed outside this phase folder is the recipe file. |
119: | REQ-005 | The spec-kit suite summary matches the 054 phase 001 start summary, or the phase records the substitution when that file is absent. |
120: 
121: ### P1 - Required (complete OR user-approved deferral)
122: 
123: | ID | Requirement |
124: |----|-------------|
125: | REQ-006 | One read-only frontier review ran at close and each finding is applied or recorded in `goal.md` section 4. |
126: 
127: > Acceptance criteria for these requirements live in `acceptance-criteria.md`,
128: > which is the document that decides whether this packet may close.
129: <!-- /ANCHOR:requirements -->
130:

132:

134: ## 5. SUCCESS CRITERIA
135: 
136: - **SC-001**: A reader who copies Step 2 gets a working `mv` command without inventing a destination.
137: - **SC-002**: The remaining `<folder>` placeholders are named with file and line, so a later packet can pick them up without a new census.
138: <!-- /ANCHOR:success-criteria -->
139:

141:

143: ## 6. RISKS & DEPENDENCIES
144: 
145: | Type | Item | Impact | Mitigation |
146: |------|------|--------|------------|
147: | Dependency | 054 phase 002 `scratch/tools/apply_row.py` | No mechanical apply | T001 checks the file and stops the phase when it is missing |
148: | Dependency | 054 phase 001 `ledger.jsonl` | The `041-006` sweep has nothing to read | T005 writes `LEDGER-MISSING`, the known row still runs, and AC-003 records 0 rows |
149: | Risk | A ledger row's locator drifted after the census | The applier refuses the row | The row is recorded `BLOCKED` with the applier line, and the phase continues |
150: | Risk | The 078 example path collides with a real packet later | The example stops being an example | The added sentence says the track is an example, and the packet number is free at the start commit |
151: <!-- /ANCHOR:risks -->
152: 
153: ---
154: 
155: 
156: ## 7. NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
157: 
158: ### Performance
159: - **NFR-P01**: One applier call per row. No model edits the recipe, so a row costs milliseconds.
160: 
161: ### Security
162: - **NFR-S01**: No brief holds a credential. The frontier review runs with `--sandbox read-only`.
163: 
164: ### Reliability
165: - **NFR-R01**: A second apply of the same row prints `FAIL <id>: locator found 0 times` and exits 1.
166: 
167: ---
168: 
169: ## 8. EDGE CASES
170: 
171: ### Data Boundaries
172: - Empty input: a ledger with no `041-006` row writes the single line `LEDGER-MISSING` or no lines, and the phase continues.
173: - Maximum length: a locator that spans four lines is one string, and the applier counts it as one occurrence.
174: 
175: ### Error Scenarios
176: - External service failure: the review dispatch fails. The error is saved to `scratch/review/T009.err` and REQ-006 stays open.
177: - Network timeout: the applier is local and has no network path.

199: | R-002 | The added sentence drifts from the file's voice | L | L | T009 checks for em dash and semicolon |
